entries.dictionary: デジタル大辞泉; 精選版 日本国語大辞典
entries.heading: じゅ【儒】
entries.evidence: Daijisen distinguishes Confucius-associated thought and a Confucian scholar. Nikkoku describes the moral/political tradition and a scholar versed in it, extending to a learned person.
entries.decision: Centre practical teaching on Confucian thought and scholars, not every Chinese person, every teacher or every religion. Do not claim that generic scholarship is impossible in every historical context. The heading and frozen character record support ジュ; no kun reading or nanori is introduced.
entries.limits: Jitsu returned attribution only: no shape history, phonetic derivation or ancient-form analysis verified. Use an explicitly invented modern-shape mnemonic.

entries.dictionary: 改訂新版 世界大百科事典
entries.heading: 儒教 (じゅきょう), Rú jiào
entries.evidence: The returned opening definition treats 儒教 as the Chinese tradition of teachings associated with the Confucian school. Its opening discussion calls 儒学 the scholarly aspect. The complete frozen JMdict 1329510 gives exact 儒教 じゅきょう, Confucianism, without spelling/reading/sense restrictions.
entries.decision: One necessary support article can teach Confucianism and the transparent ジュ + キョウ compound. Teach 教 as teaching/doctrine here, not a claim that the English religion label settles all philosophical classifications. Ordinary learning/about-history example sentences need no exhaustive chronology.
entries.limits: The first fetch returned only a bounded opening portion; the tool's saved response was truncated during viewing. A second fetch at character13000 returned a later Japanese-history portion. No complete public-page read or other dictionary section is claimed. Historical chronologies, cultural generalizations and the later evaluative historical discussion are not adopted.

entries.dictionary: 精選版 日本国語大辞典; 日本大百科全書; 山川 日本史小辞典 改訂新版
entries.heading: じゅ‐がく【儒学】; 儒学 じゅがく
entries.evidence: Nikkoku identifies the traditional learning associated with Confucius. Nipponica's opening definition distinguishes the scholarly/doctrinal aspect but explicitly notes frequent synonymous use with 儒教. Yamakawa explains the name from emphasis on teachings and classical study.
entries.decision: A qualified 儒学 comparison is useful but does not require another article for the same sole reading. Do not manufacture a strict religion-versus-secular-philosophy divide or claim the two words cannot overlap.
entries.limits: Daijisen and Jitsu returned attribution only. The bounded7000-character response was truncated near its end; no complete encyclopedia-history review is claimed. Conflicting transmission chronologies elsewhere on the page are outside the teaching scope.
